title: Briefing for 2026-11-09
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-11-09: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: China wholesale inflation hits over four-year high as consumer measure slows. U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%. The October jobs report is out Friday. Here's everything to expect. Here's what the Democratic election rout could mean for the U.S. economy. Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war, warns inflation will near 5%. Voters say the economy drove them to the polls — and blame Trump for their troubles.
global: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says. Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests. Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes. 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years. Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse. Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour.
philippines: DFA: Philippine officials’ comments on China issue ‘regrettable’. Expanded Bayanihan SIM project eyed. Department of Agriculture bans imported pork cuts. Bill vs AI job displacement filed.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
